answer: A stake-bonded registry makes fake identities expensive: each agent locks a refundable deposit before it can transact, and proven Sybil behavior slashes that bond. Like a glacier grinding slowly forward, the cost accumulates with every fake account, so an attacker faces a rising plume of expense instead of free copies. A spiral of escalating deposits for suspicious clusters, where new accounts vouch only for each other, prices out mass forgery while honest newcomers pay just one modest bond.
